q: What is Central dogma (DNA → RNA → Protein)?
a: The overall flow of genetic information in cells.
1) What “unity” means (core idea) Unity means everything works together as a whole.
A habitat is the natural place where an organism lives.
A double helix is the three-dimensional shape of DNA.
1) Literal meaning (physical) Stumbling literally means losing balance while walking—often because your foot hits an obstacle (a rock, step, root), causing you to almost fall or take awkward steps.
An organism is any individual living thing.
1) What DNA is (core idea) DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) is the molecule that stores genetic information in almost all living organisms.
A gene is a specific segment of DNA that contains the instructions to make a functional product—usually a protein, or sometimes a functional RNA molecule.
Ethical describes actions, decisions, or rules that follow moral principles—what is considered right, fair, and responsible.
1) What “inherited traits” means Inherited traits are characteristics passed from parents to offspring through genes.
A Punnett square is a diagram used to predict the possible genetic outcomes of a cross between two parents.
A claim is a statement that asserts something is true.
1) What “perspectives” means (core idea) Perspectives are the ways people see, understand, or interpret a situation, issue, or event.
1) What “reinforcement” means (core idea) Reinforcement is anything that increases the likelihood that a behavior will happen again in the future.
1) What “eukaryotic” means (core definition) Eukaryotic describes cells or organisms whose cells have a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
1) What interphase is (core idea) Interphase is the longest stage of the cell cycle, when a cell is not dividing but is actively growing, copying DNA, and preparing for division.
1) What mitosis is (core idea) Mitosis is the process by which a cell divides its nucleus to produce two genetically identical daughter cells.
1) What cytokinesis is (core idea) Cytokinesis is the final step of cell division in which the cytoplasm splits, producing two separate daughter cells.
When a cell is dividing, chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes.
1) What meiosis is (core idea) Meiosis is a type of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half, producing four genetically unique haploid cells (gametes).
1) What homologous means (core idea) Homologous means “similar in structure and function because of shared origin.”
1) What crossing over is Crossing over is the exchange of DNA segments between homologous chromosomes during meiosis.
A zygote is the single cell formed when a sperm cell fuses with an egg cell during fertilization.
A gamete is a sex cell used in sexual reproduction.
1) What haploid means (core definition) Haploid describes a cell that contains one complete set of chromosomes, written as n.
1) What diploid means (core definition) Diploid describes a cell that contains two complete sets of chromosomes, written as 2n—one set inherited from each parent.
1) What sperm is (core definition) Sperm is the male gamete (sex cell) used in sexual reproduction.
